tasks.title: HANGS Construction Services · FY2026 Subsequent Events and Going Concern
tasks.description: Review what happened to HANGS Construction Services LLC between its June 30, 2026 year end and the expected report date, October 22, 2026, and evaluate its ability to continue as a going concern, from 13 Excel, Word and PDF files: the FY2026 trial balance, the September 30 books and contract schedule, the draft notes, the board’s minutes, management’s answers, the lawyers’ letter, the cash received and paid after the year end, the loan covenants, Cinderbrook Bank’s commitment letter and the cash forecast. Classify every event as recognized or disclosed, test the covenant headroom and the forecast, and weigh management’s plans. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.outputsPath: Outputs/HANGS Construction Services FY2026 Subsequent Events
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings memo, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.

lines.text: The draft note says management found no conditions or events that raise substantial doubt. That is not what happened: they raised it, and the plans alleviate it. ASC 205-40 then requires the note to describe the conditions, management’s evaluation of their significance and the plans that alleviate the doubt (GC-01). Proposed wording for the CPA: “conditions and events … raised substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the financial statements are available to be issued … management’s plans … alleviate the substantial doubt.” Not “substantial doubt exists”, which belongs only where the plans do not alleviate it and which would put a going concern section in the report. With the doubt alleviated, AU-C 570 calls for no going concern section; the CPA may add an emphasis-of-matter paragraph.
